title: Straw Man — high confidence
input:
COUNCILMEMBER A: I think we should pilot a four-day work week for city staff, just for six months, to see the data.
COUNCILMEMBER B: So you want to dismantle the entire structure of public service and let government grind to a halt?

findings.span: So you want to dismantle the entire structure of public service and let government grind to a halt?
findings.explanation: Councilmember B recasts a limited six-month pilot as total dismantling of public service — a much stronger position than A proposed, then attacks that distortion.
findings.what_would_strengthen_this: A direct response would need to address whether a time-limited pilot can be evaluated without permanently restructuring service — the reply instead argues against a position A did not take.

notes: Canonical high-confidence positive: distortion is explicit across two speaker turns.

title: Hedged empirical claim — empty findings
input:
HOST: Does the new study settle the debate on saturated fat?
GUEST: Not really — it's one cohort study, fairly large, but observational, so it shows an association, not causation. We'd want a few replications and ideally an RCT before treating this as settled.
notes: Clean reasoning: names design limits, avoids causal leap, states what evidence would still be needed. Correct output is empty findings.

title: Appeal to Tradition vs anecdote — low confidence
input:
HOST: Some pediatricians recommend limiting screen time to one hour on weekdays.
GUEST: I get why people say that, but my grandparents didn't have screens at all and they turned out fine, so I don't think an hour a day is going to hurt anyone.

findings.span: my grandparents didn't have screens at all and they turned out fine, so I don't think an hour a day is going to hurt anyone
findings.explanation: The guest leans on how things were done in a prior generation as a reason to dismiss current guidance. A hasty-generalization read (one family's anecdote) is also plausible, but the 'didn't have screens / turned out fine' framing tracks appeal to tradition more closely.
findings.what_would_strengthen_this: Pediatric outcome data comparing screen-time thresholds to developmental or health markers would be needed — generational anecdote alone does not establish that an hour a day is harmless.

notes: Borderline case: one primary label at low confidence; explanation acknowledges the alternate read without stacking a second finding.

title: what_would_strengthen_this — gap diagnosis, not a rewrite
input:
HOST: So critics say the supplement industry isn't well regulated.
GUEST: Look, I've been taking this stuff for three years and I feel incredible. My energy's up, my focus is up. That's all the proof I need.

findings.span: I've been taking this stuff for three years and I feel incredible. My energy's up, my focus is up. That's all the proof I need.
findings.explanation: The guest treats personal experience over three years as sufficient proof for a general claim about the product, dismissing the need for broader evidence.
findings.what_would_strengthen_this: Controlled studies or population-level outcome data would be needed — personal experience alone cannot establish general efficacy or regulatory adequacy.

anti_pattern.what_would_strengthen_this: Try: 'In a randomized trial of 200 participants, 68% reported improved energy after twelve weeks, compared with 41% on placebo.'
anti_pattern.why_wrong: This drafts replacement prose the user could paste into the document. The field must name the missing evidence type, not supply the sentence.

notes: Same finding as example output; anti_pattern shows the common failure mode for what_would_strengthen_this.
